Loopy, swept and England win the second ODI by 6 wickets! A relieved Jos Buttler 
shakes hands with the opposition with a smile on his face. Runs for him, Brook and Will 
Jacks help England topple their target of 203 with 103 balls to spare. 
7.13pm The batters saw it home, but it was the bowlers who set-up this victory, 
dismissing West Indies for what looked about 70 under par. Sam Curran's three up top, 
Liam Livingstone's three in the middle - including Shai Hope - and a couple each for Gus 
Atkinson and Rehan Ahmed did the business. All to play for heading to Barbados on 
Saturday. 
7.22pm Sam Curran is player of the match. "It was a tough day the other day, but you 
need to keep moving forward and bounce back," he says. "We did so many things right 
in that first game. The messages from the coaches and captain was just that. We had 
to come back today and put things right, which we did." 
7.26pm Jos Buttler on becoming the 5th Englishman to pass 5,000 ODI runs: "Really 
pleasing. I've been playing for a while now so it's great when you get to those 
milestones after playing for a long period of time. It's been a frustrating time recently." 
7.29pm Right, that's all from us here tonight. Join us on Saturday for the decider at the 
Kensington Oval. As West Indies captain Shai Hope put it: "It's simple - we win the game, 
we win the series."
